profiles.name: English
profiles.historical_orthography_notes: Preserve supplied historical spelling; modernization is derivative.
profiles.normalization_policy: Unicode normalization may aid indexing but never replaces the supplied form.
profiles.transliteration_policy: Not normally applicable; any script conversion remains derivative.

profiles.name: Latin
profiles.historical_orthography_notes: Preserve diplomatic and normalized layers, long-s controls, u/v and i/j distinctions, abbreviations, and line-end divisions.
profiles.normalization_policy: Historical spelling transformations must remain labeled comparison forms.

profiles.name: Greek
profiles.historical_orthography_notes: Preserve supplied accents, breathings, typography, and uncertain characters.
profiles.normalization_policy: Accent-insensitive forms are candidate-retrieval aids only and cannot overwrite the source.
profiles.transliteration_policy: Transliteration remains derivative and retains Greek-source ancestry.

profiles.name: Hebrew
profiles.historical_orthography_notes: Preserve pointed or unpointed state, consonants, matres, and uncertain characters.
profiles.normalization_policy: Do not add or remove pointing for wording-sensitive analysis.
profiles.transliteration_policy: Transliteration remains derivative and is not Hebrew textual evidence.

profiles.name: German
profiles.historical_orthography_notes: Preserve historical spelling; Fraktur is a typographic source-form condition, not a language.
profiles.normalization_policy: Modern spelling is a derivative representation.
profiles.transliteration_policy: Typeface conversion or character regularization remains derivative.

profiles.name: French
profiles.historical_orthography_notes: Preserve historical spelling and lexical variation.
profiles.normalization_policy: Modern French and English translations remain derivative.

profiles.name: Dutch
profiles.historical_orthography_notes: Preserve historical spelling and source-form differences.
profiles.normalization_policy: Modern Dutch spelling remains a derivative representation.
